item.text:
# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.3 evidence note

Bottom line: I found limited but meaningful favorable evidence that Pakistan maintained and publicized a centralized nuclear security architecture during Sharif’s 2024 term. I did not find credible 2024 evidence of Sharif weakening custody, command discipline, or accident-prevention safeguards. The record is mostly institutional and indirect, not a clean set of ruler-specific operational actions.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program is for peaceful purposes, for self-defense, and has no aggressive designs. This is not a technical safeguard announcement, but it is a direct public stewardship statement consistent with disciplined custody and non-escalatory control of nuclear assets. | 1B.3; also 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Favorable / indirect | Pakistan's Nuclear Safety & Security Regime | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05 | https://www.mofa.gov.pk/vienna-pakistans-nuclear-safety-seccurity-regime | Pakistan’s official nuclear-security page says the NCA is chaired by the prime minister, the SPD serves as secretariat, and in May 2024 Pakistan published an updated nuclear security regime booklet and a practical arrangement with the IAEA. This is the strongest 2024 evidence of command-and-control and safeguards architecture during Sharif’s term, though it is institutional rather than a personal action by him. | 1B.3 |
| Favorable / indirect | Pakistan’s election as the President for the Tenth Review Meeting of the Convention on Nuclear Safety (CNS) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistans-election-as-chair-of-convention-on-nuclear-security-cns | Pakistan said the election of PNRA chairman Faizan Mansoor as CNS president reflected international trust in Pakistan’s nuclear-safety record. This supports an inference that the safety and oversight regime remained credible in 2024 under Sharif’s government, though it does not prove any specific new safeguard initiative by him. | 1B.3 |

## Search gap

- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of Sharif personally issuing a new command-and-control reform, custody protocol, or accident-prevention directive.
- I also did not find reliable 2024 evidence of a safeguard failure, custody lapse, or public controversy over nuclear safety under his watch.
- So the best-supported reading is mildly favorable but low-confidence: the available material points to continued institutional discipline, not clearly documented new strengthening by Sharif himself.
